recipes.name: Feast inspired by Chef
ingredients: For the Sous Vide Pork Belly
1 dried ancho chile, stem and seeds removed
To taste freshly ground black pepper
1 tsp kosher salt + more to taste
To taste freshly ground black pepper
For the Korean Octopus Stir Fry
1 tbsp sesame oil + more to finish
5 green onions, chopped + more to garnish
For the Dry Aged Ribeye Steak
As needed freshly ground black pepper
To taste freshly ground black pepper
For the Butter Roasted Fingerling Potatoes
To taste freshly ground black pepper
To taste freshly ground black pepper
To taste freshly ground black pepper
1/2 cup good quality heavy cream, cold
1 tsp vanilla paste (or 1/2 tsp vanilla extract)
instructions: For the Sous Vide Pork Belly
Tear the ancho chile into 1-inch pieces. - 1 dried ancho chile stem and seeds removed
In a medium skillet, toast the chile over medium-high heat.
Add water to the toasted ancho chile. Bring the water to a simmer, then turn off the heat and cover the pot. Allow the mixture to steep for 15 minutes. - 1 cup water divided
Pour the steeped liquid and the chile into a blender. Add the ice cubes and remaining half cup of water and blend until smooth. - ½ cup water divided - ⅓ cup ice cubes

Pour the blended liquid into a bowl and add the remaining ingredients to the bowl, save for the pork belly. Whisk to thoroughly combine the brine. - 1 Juice of orange - 2 Juice of limes - 5 cloves garlic crushed - 3 dried bay leaves - 2 sticks Mexican cinnamon - 1 tbsp Mexican oregano - 1 tbsp black peppercorns - 1 tbsp (packed) brown sugar - 2 tbsp soy sauce - 2 tbsp mirin - 2 tbsp kosher salt

Pour the brine into a zip-top bag. Add the pork belly and seal the bag. Massage the bag to ensure all parts of the pork belly are covered by the brine. *If the pork belly is too large to fit in the bag, slice it in half. - 4 ½ lbs pork belly skin removed
Refrigerate the pork belly overnight or up to 24 hours.
Prepare the sous vide and set the temperature to 165 °F.
While the water is coming up to temperature, remove the pork belly from the marinade and rinse it off. Pat the pork belly dry and vacuum pack.
Gently place the vac-packed pork into the water and cook for 10 hours.
Transfer the pork belly from the vacuum bag and onto a grill rack placed in a sheet tray.
Brush a generous coating of the garlic chili sauce onto the top of the pork belly. Broil until the pork belly is crispy, about 4-6 minutes. - Garlic Chili Sauce (see recipe below)

Serve with the carrot puree, salsa verde, pickled radish, and sliced scallions. - Carrot Puree (see recipe below) - Salsa Verde (see recipe below) - Pickled Radish (see recipe below) - To garnish: scallions thinly sliced
For the Garlic Chili Sauce

Combine all of the ingredients in a small bowl. - ⅓ cup gochujang - ¼ cup soy sauce - ¼ cup honey - 3 tbsp brown sugar - 4 garlic cloves minced - 1 tbsp freshly grated ginger - To taste kosher salt - To taste freshly ground black pepper
Whisk until well combined. Reserve until ready to use.
For the Carrot Puree
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
In a small bowl, coat the garlic in the oil. Transfer the garlic to a piece of aluminum foil, wrap the foil around the garlic. - 1 small head garlic - 1 tsp neutral oil
Roast the garlic in the preheated oven for 35-45 minutes or until completely tender.

Meanwhile, combine the water, carrots, and salt in a medium pot. Bring the water to a boil, then cover the pot, and reduce the heat to medium-low. Simmer the carrots for 20-25 minutes or until completely tender. - 1 ½ cup water - 1 lb heirloom carrots peeled + sliced - 1 tsp kosher salt + more to taste

Transfer the cooked carrots to a blender. Add the garlic, cumin, brown sugar, lemon juice, and ½ cup of the carrot cooking liquid. While blending, stream in the olive oil. Continue blending until the mixture is completely smooth, add more water if necessary. - ¼ tsp ground cumin - 1 tbsp (packed) brown sugar - 1 tbsp freshly squeezed lemon juice - 1 tbsp olive oil
Season the puree to taste with salt and pepper. Keep warm until ready to serve. - kosher salt + more to taste - To taste freshly ground black pepper
For the Salsa Verde

Add the tomatillos, onion, peppers, and garlic to a sheet tray. Coat them in vegetable oil. - 6 tomatillos peeled + halved - 1 small white onion quartered - 3 cloves garlic - 2 serrano peppers stem removed + halved - 1 tbsp vegetable oil divided
Broil the vegetables for 3-5 minutes or until charred.
Allow the vegetables to cool slightly.
Transfer the charred vegetables, lime juice, and cilantro to a high-powered blender. Blend the sauce is completely smooth - 1 Juice of lime - ⅓ cup cilantro leaves
Season the sauce to taste with salt and reserve until ready to use. - To taste kosher salt
For the Pickled Radish
Place the radishes and mustard seeds in a medium bowl. - 7 radishes thinly sliced - 1 tsp yellow mustard seeds - ¼ tsp Optional: red pepper flakes
Combine the water, sugar, vinegar, and salt in a small pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer. - ½ cup water - ¼ cup granulated sugar - ¼ cup white vinegar - ½ tsp kosher salt
Pour the vinegar solution over the radishes. Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until ready to use.
For the Korean Octopus Stir Fry
If necessary, remove the intestines, beak, and eyes from the octopus. - 1 lb baby octopus cleaned
Blanch the octopus in boiling water until opaque and the tentacles have curled, about 1 minute.

In a small bowl, combine the gochujang, gochugaru, black pepper, soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil. - 2 tbsp gochujang - 1 tbsp gochugaru - ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper - 1 ½ tbsp soy sauce - 1 tbsp granulated sugar - 1 tbsp sesame oil + more to finish
Heat the neutral oil in a large wok over medium-high heat. - 2 tbsp neutral oil
Add the onion and cabbage and cook for 3-4 minutes. - ½ white onion sliced - ½ green cabbage sliced
Add the chili and green onion and cook for 1-2 minutes. - 1 green chili (spicy or mild) sliced - 5 green onions chopped + more to garnish

Add the octopus and reserved sauce. Stir to combine everything. Cook for 1-2 minutes, then turn off the heat and finish with a drizzle of sesame oil and a sprinkling of sesame seeds. - 1 tsp white sesame seeds - sesame oil + more to finish
Garnish with thinly sliced green onion and serve. - green onions chopped + more to garnish
For the Dry Aged Ribeye Steak
Thirty minutes before cooking, place the steak on a sheet tray. Season it generously with salt and pepper. - Dry Aged Ribeye Steak - As needed kosher salt - As needed freshly ground black pepper
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Preheat a large cast iron skillet with the oil over high heat. - 1 tbsp neutral oil
Sear the steak on one side, about 3-4 minutes.

Flip the steak, then add the butter, thyme, and garlic. Baste the steak with the melted butter for about 3-4 minutes or until the other side of the steak has a nice crust. - 3 tbsp unsalted butter cubed - 4 ½ thyme sprigs - 2 cloves garlic

Transfer the steak to a grill rack placed in a rimmed baking sheet. Place the steak in the preheated oven to finish cooking, about 10-15 minutes. The internal temperature of the steak should reach 135°F.
Allow the steak to rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
Serve the steak with lemon, cilantro, roe, and creme fraiche. - 1 lemon halved - whole Cilantro leaves - Salmon roe - Creme fraiche
For the Sumac Charred Cauliflower
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Cut the head of the cauliflower into florets. - ½ head cauliflower
Toss the cauliflower in oil, salt, pepper, and sumac. - As need neutral oil - To taste kosher salt - To taste freshly ground black pepper - ½ tsp sumac
Transfer the cauliflower to a sheet tray and bake until cooked through, about 15-20 minutes.
Serve immediately.
For the Butter Roasted Fingerling Potatoes
Preheat the oven to 425°F. Place a quarter sheet tray inside the oven to preheat as well.
Slice the potatoes in half lengthwise. - 1 lb fingerling potatoes washed
Bring a large pot of water to boil. Season the water with the vinegar and salt. - 1 tbsp white vinegar - 2 tsp To taste kosher salt
Par-boil the potatoes, about 10 minutes, then drain the potatoes.
Coat the potatoes in the butter. - 3 tbsp unsalted butter melted
Transfer the potatoes to the preheated sheet tray, make sure to place the potatoes cut-side down.
Bake the potatoes for 20-25 minutes or until crispy and the bottoms are well browned.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. - To taste kosher salt - To taste freshly ground black pepper
For the Grilled Lime Corn
Coat the corn in oil. - 2 ears corn shucked - As needed neutral oil
Char corn on the grill, about 4-5 minutes.
Allow the corn to cool slightly, then cut the kernels off the cob.
Season the kernels with salt, pepper, and lime juice. - To taste kosher salt - To taste freshly ground black pepper - 1 Juice of lime
Reserved until ready to serve.
For the Lemon Squash Salad
Slice the zucchini lengthwise using a mandolin. - 2 green zucchini
Coat the zucchini in oil, then grill until tender, about 3-4 minutes. - Oil as needed
Serve the grilled squash with a few sprigs of fresh lemon verbena, and season with salt and pepper. - 3 ½ fresh lemon verbena leaves - To taste kosher salt - To taste freshly ground black pepper
For the Macerated Berries

Combine the berries, sugar, and mint in a large bowl. Allow the mixture to sit at room temperature for 30 minutes. - 1 pint blueberries washed - 1 pint blackberries washed - 1 pint raspberries washed - ¼ cup granulated sugar - ¼ cup fresh mint thinly sliced
Transfer the berry mixture to a serving bowl and garnish with whipped cream and caramel dust. - Whipped Cream (see recipe below) - Caramel Dust (see recipe below)
For the Whipped Cream
Combine all of the ingredients in a large bowl. - ½ cup good quality heavy cream cold - 2 tbsp powdered sugar - 1 tsp vanilla paste (or 1/2 tsp vanilla extract)
Whisk the mixture by hand until thickened to your liking.
Reserve in the refrigerator for up to 1 hour before serving.
For the Caramel Dust
Prepare a sheet tray with a silicone baking mat.
Combine the sugar and corn syrup in a large skillet. - 1 cup white granulated sugar - 1 tbsp corn syrup
Over medium heat, begin melting the sugar. Once the outside begins to liquefy, begin swirling the sugar to evenly distribute the heat.
Once all of the sugar has melted, continue cooking until it reaches a light amber color.
Pour the caramel over the prepared baking sheet. Allow the caramel to cool completely.
Bake the caramel into shards, then transfer them to a clean kitchen towel. Fold the towel to cover the caramel shards. Using a meat mallet, smash the caramel.
Transfer the caramel to a sieve over a bowl. Sift the caramel.
Reserved the caramel dust and use it immediately.
